nodes.title: 3. Script: one turn per line, Name: text
4. Speech for every line: model and language here

widgets_values:
## Talking characters with subtitles

A picture and a short script become a video of the characters speaking it, with the lines burned in as subtitles and saved as an .srt file.

1. **Picture**: load an image showing the characters, or keep the sample.
2. **Voices**: describe each voice in plain words. Voice 1 belongs to whoever speaks first in the script, voice 2 to the second. To use recordings of real voices instead, switch on *Use my own recordings* and load 6 to 15 seconds of each voice.
3. **Script**: one turn per line, written as `Name: text`. Two voices are wired; a third name stops the run with a message.
4. **Language**: a Finnish script runs on the Finnish model as set. For another language set `model` in the speech node to the multilingual model, pick the `language` and set `cfg_weight` to 0, so the English designed voices bring no English accent.
5. **Video prompt**: describe the scene and who speaks when, for example who stands on the left and who talks first.
6. Run. The video is as long as the dialogue.

Outputs: the video with and without subtitles and the .srt in `output/video/`, the dialogue audio in `output/audio/`. If a line comes back empty or far longer than its text, the run stops and names it. Burned-in subtitles draw Latin, Greek and Cyrillic letters; for the other scripts use the .srt.

Keep one scene under about 15 seconds and split longer conversations into several runs. Other languages Chatterbox speaks: Arabic, Chinese, Danish, Dutch, English, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swahili, Swedish, Turkish.
nodes.title: How to use

widgets_values:
## About this workflow

Built for this repo from five parts:
- Voice design: Qwen3-TTS 1.7B VoiceDesign through 1038lab's [ComfyUI-QwenTTS](https://github.com/1038lab/ComfyUI-QwenTTS) (GPL-3.0). Qwen3-TTS speaks ten languages, so the voices are designed in English and the next step carries them into the script's language.
- Speech: Finnish-NLP's [Chatterbox-Finnish](https://huggingface.co/Finnish-NLP/Chatterbox-Finnish) (MIT) for Finnish, Resemble AI's Chatterbox multilingual model (MIT) for the other languages. The Finnish model is Finnish-NLP's fine-tune of the multilingual one on 16,604 Finnish clips. On Finnish speakers it was not trained on, its authors measured 2.76 % word errors, against 28.94 % for the multilingual model it started from. Chatterbox Speech, a node of this repo's template pack, runs both with the Chatterbox code in filliptm's [ComfyUI_Fill-ChatterBox](https://github.com/filliptm/ComfyUI_Fill-ChatterBox) (MIT). It samples with upstream Chatterbox's alignment check, which ends each line once the text has been read; that pack's own nodes leave it out, and the multilingual model then talked on after most lines.
- Dialogue Script, Join Dialogue, Burn In Subtitles and Save Subtitles from this repo's template pack. The subtitles come from the script and the clip lengths, so their text and timing are exact.
- Video: the LTX-2.5 audio to video graph from Lightricks' ComfyUI-LTXVideo (LTX-2 Community License), set up as in this repo's *Audio to Video (LTX-2.5)*: int8 transformer and text encoder, local prompt path only.
- Putting a generated voice on a talking character with LTX follows RuneXX's LTX-2.3 *Talking Avatar* workflows in [RuneXX/LTX-2.3-Workflows](https://huggingface.co/RuneXX/LTX-2.3-Workflows).

Sample picture `two_character_talking.png` from Comfy's template inputs.
